Subject: Quantifying peak & surge: tokens/sec profile request + initial assumptions

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the chat this morning. To make the Dedicated capacity proposal concrete for Orion Health, can you confirm the traffic envelope in the attached demand profile? For the initial sizing exercise I used the usage numbers you mentioned:

- 500k monthly active users (MAU)
- Average session: 6 completions
- Median prompt size: ~120 tokens; average completion length: ~220 tokens

That maps to a steady-state token rate estimate of ~2.1M tokens/day (~24 tokens/sec average across rolling 24h) but more importantly you called out burst patterns tied to morning shift handoffs and batch ingestion windows (estimated 3x–6x spike lasting 10–30m).

Questions / asks:
- Can you attach one week of per-minute traffic or confirm the surge multiplier / duration?
- Are there strict P99 latency SLOs per completion we need to match? You mentioned 2s P95 for interactive workflows, is P99 tighter?
- Any constraints on model variants we should assume (e.g., Llama-3-70B quantized vs smaller 13B families for fallback)?

I attached a draft demand profile (orion_demand_profile.xlsx) — I’ll run a couple of slab scenarios once you confirm the burst window and P99 target.

Goal for this thread: produce a short, actionable slab recommendation (GPUs reserved, burst pool sizing, fallback routing) plus a one-page ops playbook for handoffs.

Best,
Irene

Hi Irene —

Thanks — attaching the anonymized per-minute ingestion for last 7 days (see attached CSV). High-level clarifications:
- Peak mornings roughly 07:30–08:05 local (approx 35–40 minute window), we see a 4.8x multiplier vs baseline in that window on weekdays.
- We also run an hourly batch at 02:00 that causes a short 10–12 minute spike ~6x baseline.
- P95 interactive target is 2s; P99 has been softer historically (around 4s) but our product team wants to target 3s P99 for the primary workflow.
- Preferred model: we want to serve a quantized Llama-3-70B for high-quality responses but are open to smaller 13B as a cold-fallback if cost/latency require it.

Procurement will need a clear description of reserved GPU counts and a deterministic failover plan for the SLA. Ravi from CloudPartner is copied — they are scoped to help with private connectivity for the Dedicated deployment.

Claire

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantifying peak & surge: tokens/sec profile request + initial assumptions

Irene / Karthik —

I processed Claire's per-minute data and ran three deterministic scenarios (attached quick math pasted below). Assumptions:
- Model throughput: Llama-3-70B quantized on A100-80GB equiv: ~450 tokens/sec per GPU sustained for shortish completions (windowed KV cache favorable).
- Llama-3-13B quantized (fallback): ~1,200 tokens/sec per GPU.
- Average completion latency target mapped to tokens/sec throughput: to achieve P95 <= 2s and P99 <= 3s we budget for 30ms per token effective processing on average across seq length and overheads (including network/queueing).

Scenario A — Baseline (24 tokens/sec average across day):
- Required equivalent GPUs (70B): baseline steady demand = 24 tps total -> 24 / 450 = 0.055 GPUs -> effectively 1 GPU covers baseline with massive headroom.

Scenario B — Morning peak (4.8x for 40 min):
- Instantaneous tokens/sec during peak: baseline 24 * 4.8 = 115 tps -> 115 / 450 = 0.26 GPUs.
- To meet P99=3s with safety margin (x3 headroom for queue spikes and KV cache churn), recommend 1 GPU reserved for morning peak if only 70B used.

Scenario C — Batch ingestion spike (6x for 12m):
- Instantaneous: 24 * 6 = 144 tps -> 144 / 450 = 0.32 GPUs -> again fits on 1 GPU nominally, but with headroom recommend a small burst pool.

Multi-model strategy (recommended):
- Primary dedicated slab: 8 A100-equiv GPUs reserved for the ORN deal (allows room for other workloads, stable baseline, and mid-sized growth). Why 8? It gives capacity for concurrent experiments, model rollouts, and a 5–10x steady buffer vs current baseline while keeping commit administrative simplicity.
- Burst pool: 2 extra GPUs (preemptible or reserved at lower commit tier) to absorb simultaneous morning peaks + batch overlap. These can be set on automated policy to spin up for 10–40 minute windows and tear down.
- Fallback routing: if slab utilization exceeds 80% for >2 minutes, route new sessions to 13B quantized endpoints (in the same region) — this gives >3x per-GPU throughput cost-effectively while lowering latency tail risk.

Headroom math summary (quick):
- Steady tokens/sec headroom with 8 GPUs @ 450 tps each = 8 * 450 = 3,600 tps -> 150x current baseline average.
- Morning peak at 4.8x is ~115 tps; even with 100 concurrent heavy completions you'd stay well under capacity.

Operational notes:
- We should surface per-token cost delta in the proposal: 70B quantized per-token cost x~2.8 vs 13B (ballpark) — will prepare cost delta slide.
- SLA: if Orion requires firm P99=3s with financial credits for misses, we need a locked commit at 8 GPUs plus a documented fallback chain and a playbook for on-call scaling.

Next steps: Karthik can turn these numbers into an SLO-fit matrix and a monthly cost estimate; Irene, can you lock the 2-week legal window with Procurement so we can iterate on commit language?

Ben

Hi Claire — thanks for the data and team — summary proposal below. Quoted bullets map directly to contractual and ops asks so Procurement has a crisp deliverable.

Proposed Dedicated commitment (recommended for ORN-2027-015):
- Reserved slab: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (region: us-west-2) — deterministic SLA boundary for P99=3s on primary 70B quantized model when combined with fallbacks and KV caching.
- Burst pool: 2 GPUs configured as fast-burst (policy-driven; spin-up within 90s) for short windows (10–40m) tied to morning and batch spikes.
- Fallback chain: primary -> 70B quantized (on slab) | if slab utilization >80% sustained >2m -> route new sessions to 13B quantized endpoints (hosted or shared capacity) | if region capacity constrained -> fall back to regional read-only cache with degraded responses (documented).
- Ops playbook: short runbook for on-call to manually trigger extra burst capacity and for monitoring token-level cost. I attached a one-page playbook draft in the drive link.

Cost / SLAs:
- Estimated monthly baseline commit: see attached draft_multipool_commit.docx — will provide line-item monthly cost and token-rate pricing per model in the next 24h.
- If Orion requires financial credits for P99 misses, Procurement please share the procurement timeline and any preferred SLA language; we can map credits to latency tier and hit target on commit sizing.

Ask from Orion for procurement and engineering:
1) Approve 8 GPU reserved slab + 2 GPU burst pool as the baseline for legal review.
2) Confirm ability to accept automated fallback to 13B quantized endpoints for tail-risk.
3) Procure: a 14-day review window to finalize multipool commit wording; we will provide cost delta and runbook updates within 48h.

If that sounds sensible I’ll spin up a short proposal doc and an ops playbook and circulate to Procurement for sign-off.

Thanks — we’ll keep the numbers conservative and include explicit headroom math in the proposal.

Irene
